newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF expects no more Kizu-sized failures -- Jiji.
newsitem.headline: MOF expects no more Kizu-sized failures -- Jiji.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) expects no more large financial failures on the scale of that of Kizu Shinyo Kumiai, a regional credit union that failed in 1995, Jiji News Agency quoted a senior MOF official as saying on Friday.
"We do not expect a large failure on the scale of Kizu," Kimio Yamaguchi, director-general of the Finance Ministry's Banking Bureau, was quoted as telling a parliamentary financial committee.

Speaking on Japan's bad loans problem, Yamaguchi also told the committee that, "it is a major prerequisite that financial institutions do their utmost to restructure and that the burden is kept within the financial system," Jiji said.
